summary: Anna Filigenzi works in archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A member of the Italian Institute for Africa and the East (1984), she directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003) and held posts at Naples "L'Orientale" (~2012) and Federico II (2021).

Anna Halafoff is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a BA from the University of Melbourne, a Master of Letters from the University of New England, and a PhD from Monash University, and holds a post at Deakin University.

Anna Kamensky (1867–1952) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at the Bestuzhev Courses, she earned her Ph.D. at the University of Geneva (~1923–1926), where she later served as Privatdozent in comparative religion (~1928–1950).

Anna Kramskova works in Tibetology and linguistics. She completed her magister degree at Saint Petersburg State University (2014–2016) and served as a research assistant at the Institute of Linguistic Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 2019.

Anna M. Shields (born 1966) is a Sinologist. She held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) before becoming a Professor at Princeton University in 2015. She also taught Thomas James Mazanec.

Anna Sawerthal specializes in Tibetology. She earned an MA at the University of Vienna under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes, alongside teachers Johanna Buß, Dawa Tsering, and Norbu Tashi, and completed her PhD at Heidelberg University.
Anna Scarabel is an Indologist who completed her Ph.D. at Heidelberg University in 2018. Her faculty affiliation at the University of Vienna is attested for 2026.

Anna Seidel (1938–1991) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studying under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. A member of the EFEO (1969), she held posts at Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1969–1991) and founded Cahiers d'Extrême-Asie in 1985.

Anna Stirr works in Indology. Educated at Lawrence University (BA 1998–2002) and Columbia University (PhD 2003–2009), she held appointments at The New School (2009), Oxford (2009–2011), Leiden (2011), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2012).

Anna Szabolcsi (born 1953) is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (Ph.D.). She held posts at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (~1976–1990), UCLA (~1990–1998), and New York University (~1998).
Anna Šebestová was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at Charles University in 1919 under the doctoral supervision of Josef Zubatý.

Anna-Pya Sjödin specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007 under supervisors Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, having also studied under Barbro Eriksson.
Annarao Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held posts at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Anncharlott Eschmann (1941–1977) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. After studies in Munich and Marburg, she earned her Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (1961–1969), where she later became an assistant in 1975.
Anne Burchardi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Erik Haarh. She has held a post at the National Museum of Denmark.

Anne Carolyn Klein (born 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, earning a PhD from the University of Virginia (~1974–1981). A professor at Rice University from ~1987, she also co-founded the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism.

Anne E. Monius (1964–2019) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her degrees at Harvard, taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002), and served as professor of South Asian Religions at Harvard from 2002.

Anne Feldhaus (born 1949) specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Manhattanville University and the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. ~1971–1976), and was appointed a professor of religious studies at Arizona State University in 1981.

Anne Hardgrove is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Carleton College (~1986–1990) and the University of Michigan (~1991–1999), she joined the history faculty at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.

Anne Hopkins Aitken (1911–1994) was active in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Scripps College, Stanford, Northwestern, and Oxford, and co-founded the Honolulu Diamond Sangha in 1959 as well as the Maui Zendo.
